facts.statement: Pteranodon gigas is a synonym of Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Pteranodon gigas Lawson, 1972

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus lawsoni was described by Andres and Langston Jr. in 2021.
facts.quote: subdivision: Q.? lawsoni Andres and Langston Jr., 2021

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus lived in North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Quetzalcoatlus () is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in North America.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Quetzalcoatlus northropi was recovered in 1971 from the Javelina Formation in Texas and described in 1975 by Douglas Lawson.
facts.quote: The type specimen, recovered in 1971 from the Javelina Formation of Texas, United States, consists of several wing fragments and was described as Quetzalcoatlus northropi in 1975 by Douglas Lawson.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Aztec god Quetzalcōātl and the species name honors Jack Northrop.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Aztec serpent god of the sky, Quetzalcōātl, while the specific name honors Jack Northrop, designer of a tailless fixed-wing aircraft.

facts.statement: Recent estimates of the wingspan of Quetzalcoatlus northropi hover around 10 to 11 meters.
facts.quote: While wingspan estimates over the years have ranged from 5.2–25.8 m, more recent estimates hover around 10 – 11 m.

facts.statement: Historical interpretations of Quetzalcoatlus diet included scavenging and skim-feeding.
facts.quote: Historical interpretations of the diet of Quetzalcoatlus have ranged from scavenging to skim-feeding like the modern skimmer bird.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests Quetzalcoatlus likely hunted small prey on the ground like storks and ground hornbills.
facts.quote: However, more recent research has found that it most likely hunted small prey on the ground, in a similar way to storks and ground hornbills.

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus lawsoni is suggested to have fed on small aquatic invertebrates near alkaline lakes.
facts.quote: On the other hand, the disputed second species, Q. lawsoni, appears to have been associated with alkaline lakes, and a diet of small aquatic invertebrates has been suggested.

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus lawsoni appears to have been highly gregarious, unlike the speculated solitary nature of Q. northropi.
facts.quote: Similarly, while Q. northropi is speculated to have been fairly solitary, Q. lawsoni appears to have been highly gregarious (social).

facts.statement: Research by Witton and Habib in 2010 suggests Quetzalcoatlus likely launched itself into the air using a four-legged posture.
facts.quote: Based on the work of Mark P. Witton and Michael Habib in 2010, it now seems likely that pterosaurs, especially larger taxa such as Quetzalcoatlus, launched quadrupedally (from a four-legged posture), using the powerful muscles of their forelimbs to propel themselves off the ground and into the air.

facts.statement: The first Quetzalcoatlus fossils were discovered in 1971 by Douglas A. Lawson during his Master's degree field work.
facts.quote: The first Quetzalcoatlus fossils were discovered in 1971 by the graduate student Douglas A. Lawson while conducting field work for his Master's degree project on the paleoecology of the Javelina Formation.

facts.statement: Lawson announced the discovery in the journal Science in March 1975, featuring a size comparison with a large aircraft and a Pteranodon on the cover.
facts.quote: Lawson announced his discovery in the journal Science in March 1975, with a depiction of the animal's size compared to a large aircraft and a Pteranodon gracing the cover of the issue.

facts.statement: Lawson stated that the animal was without doubt the largest flying animal known at the time.
facts.quote: Lawson wrote that it was "without doubt the largest flying animal presently known".

facts.statement: Lawson named the genus after the Aztec god Quetzalcōātl and the species after John Knudsen Northrop, founder of the Northrop Corporation.
facts.quote: Though not specified in the original publication, Lawson named the genus after the Aztec feathered serpent god Quetzalcōātl, while the specific name honors John Knudsen Northrop, the founder of Northrop Corporation, who drove the development of large tailless Northrop YB-49 aircraft designs resembling Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: The discovery was featured in Time Magazine and appeared on the cover of Scientific American in 1981.
facts.quote: It was featured in Time Magazine and appeared on the cover of Scientific American in 1981 alongside an article on pterosaurs by Langston.

facts.statement: Near the end of the 1974 season, Langston found a more complete pterosaur skeleton including a wing, vertebrae, and a femur.
facts.quote: Near the end of the 1974 season, Langston stumbled over a much more complete pterosaur skeleton; it consisted of a wing, multiple vertebrae, a femur and multiple other long bones.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Quetzalcoatlus lawsoni should be placed within the genus Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: Previously, smaller azhdarchid specimens were referred to the species Q. lawsoni, though other researchers have questioned the placement of this species within the genus.

facts.statement: Eight new specimens of Quetzalcoatlus were discovered in 1977.
facts.quote: Excavations continued in 1976, and eight new specimens emerged in 1977

facts.statement: Ten additional specimens were found at a new site discovered by Langston in 1979.
facts.quote: in 1979, despite complications due to losing the field notes from 1977, Langston discovered another new site that would produce an additional ten specimens

facts.statement: Several new localities yielding fossils were found in 1980.
facts.quote: Several further new localities followed in 1980

facts.statement: The last significant discoveries of Quetzalcoatlus fossils occurred during visits in 1983 and 1985.
facts.quote: visits during 1983 and 1985 proved to provide the last substantive discoveries of Quetzalcoatlus fossils

facts.statement: Langston made his final visit to the Big Bend excavation site in 1999.
facts.quote: Langston would visit Big Bend for the last time in 1999

facts.statement: In 1981, Langston questioned whether smaller individuals from Pterodactyl Ridge belonged to the same species as Quetzalcoatlus northropi.
facts.quote: In a 1981 article on pterosaurs, Langston expressed reservations whether they were truly the same species as the immense Q. northropi

facts.statement: A comprehensive description of the genus was published in 2021.
facts.quote: In 2021, a comprehensive description of the genus was finally published

facts.statement: A study debated the classical interpretation of Quetzalcoatlus as the last of a dying lineage, suggesting many lineages persisted into the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic study of Quetzacoatlus and its relationships within Pterosauria, with a focus on the persistence of many lineages into the Late Cretaceous contra classical interpretations of Quetzalcoatlus as the last of a dying lineage

facts.statement: The name Quetzalcoatlus was introduced in 1975.
facts.quote: Though the name Quetzalcoatlus was introduced in 1975

facts.statement: The oldest name for the species was "Pteranodon gigas" from a 1973 thesis by Lawson.
facts.quote: The oldest name for the species is "Pteranodon gigas", from Lawson's 1973 thesis.

facts.statement: A diagnosis for the species was provided in a 1991 paper by Lev Nessov.
facts.quote: The species received a diagnosis in a 1991 paper by Lev Nessov

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Mark Witton and colleagues questioned whether Quetzalcoatlus could be validly diagnosed.
facts.quote: a study by Mark Witton and colleagues in 2010 doubted whether Quetzalcoatlus could be validly diagnosed at all

facts.statement: A 2021 paper settled previous taxonomic issues by rediagnosing Quetzalcoatlus as distinct.
facts.quote: Both of these issues were settled in the 2021 paper, whose rediagnosis affirmed Quetzalcoatlus as distinct.

facts.statement: An ICZN petition approved on August 30, 2019, formally established Quetzalcoatlus northropi as the type species.
facts.quote: The approval of this ICZN petition on August 30, 2019, conserved and formalized the binomen Quetzalcoatlus northropi as the type species.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Q. northropi is TxVP 41450-3, which is a partial wing.
facts.quote: The name-bearing type specimen of Q. northropi is TxVP 41450-3, a partial wing.

facts.statement: The type specimen comes from the uppermost rocks of the Javelina Formation and is one of the youngest known pterosaur specimens.
facts.quote: It is from the uppermost rocks of the Javelina Formation, making it one of the youngest pterosaur specimens known.

facts.statement: Only one other specimen, a left ulna designated TxVP 44036-1 from the Black Peaks Formation, can be confidently assigned to Q. northropi.
facts.quote: Only a single other specimen can confidently be assigned to the same species, a left ulna designated TxVP 44036-1 known from the Black Peaks Formation

facts.statement: Four other giant specimens cannot be definitively assigned to Q. northropi due to a lack of overlapping material or distinguishing anatomy.
facts.quote: Four other specimens share a similarly giant size, but cannot be definitively assigned to Q. northropi in lack of overlapping material or distinguishing anatomical regions.

facts.statement: Specimens TxVP 41047-1 and TxVP 41398-3 are partial femurs, with the former being twice the size of those seen in Q. lawsoni.
facts.quote: TxVP 41047-1 and TxVP 41398-3, are both partial femurs, the former twice the size of that seen in Q. lawsoni.

facts.statement: Specimen TxVP 41398-4 is part of a wing finger of the correct size for Q. northropi but lacks essential anatomy to confirm its identity.
facts.quote: Part of a wing finger, TxVP 41398-4, is also of the correct size to belong to Q. northropi but does not preserve the essential anatomy to confirm its identity.

facts.statement: One of the oldest pterosaur specimens in Big Bend is a giant cervical vertebra that does not match smaller species from the formation.
facts.quote: Finally, one of the oldest pterosaur specimens in Big Bend is a giant cervical vertebra not matching that of smaller species from the formation.

facts.statement: While conventionally assigned to Q. northropi, a 2021 redescription assigned certain specimens to Q. cf. northropi to indicate uncertainty.
facts.quote: While conventional pterosaur research would assign all of these to Q. northropi, the 2021 redescription preferred to be cautious and merely assigned them to Q. cf. northropi, indicating uncertainty.

facts.statement: A total of 305 fossil elements from 214 specimens are known and considered consistent with assignment to Q. lawsoni.
facts.quote: In total, 305 different fossil elements from 214 specimens are known, all of which are considered consistent with assignment to the same species.

facts.statement: This represents the largest number of remains assigned to any single pterosaur species.
facts.quote: This is the most remains assigned to any singular species of pterosaur.

facts.statement: Two less complete specimens, TxVP 42180-14 and TxVP 42161-1, were preserved in partial articulation.
facts.quote: Two less complete specimens, TxVP 42180-14 and TxVP 42161-1, were also preserved in partial articulation

facts.statement: Taken together, nearly the entire skeleton of Q. lawsoni is represented, except for some of the back of the skull.
facts.quote: Taken together, nearly the entirely skeleton is represented, with the exception of some of the back of the skull.

facts.statement: In 2025, it was suggested that Quetzalcoatlus is polyphyletic and that Q. lawsoni is not the sister species to Q. northropi.
facts.quote: In 2025, Quetzalcoatlus was suggested to be polyphyletic with Quetzalcoatlus lawsoni not being sister to Quetzalcoatlus northropi.

facts.statement: A specimen designated TxVP 42489-2, consisting of a partial skull, jaws, and five neck vertebrae, was found about 380 meters north of the Pterodactyl Ridge localities.
facts.quote: Most prominent amongst these is a specimen discovered around 380 m north of the Pterodactyl Ridge localities, designated as TxVP 42489-2 and compromising a partial skull and jaws as well as five articulated neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 1982, Philip J. Currie and Dale Russell assigned a femur from the Campanian-aged Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada, to the genus Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: In 1982 a femur from the Campanian aged Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada was assigned to the genus by Philip J. Currie and Dale Russell.

facts.statement: A neck vertebra from the Maastrichtian-aged Hell Creek Formation in Montana was discovered in 2002 and initially assigned to Quetzalcoatlus in 2006.
facts.quote: A neck vertebra from the Hell Creek Formation, also from Montana but dating to the Maastrichtian, was discovered in 2002 and initially assigned in 2006 to Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: A neck vertebra from the Lance Formation in Wyoming, first described in 1964, was assigned to Quetzalcoatlus by Brent H. Breithaupt in 1982.
facts.quote: Another neck vertebra, discovered in the similarly aged Lance Formation in Wyoming and first described in 1964, was later assigned to Quetzalcoatlus by Brent H. Breithaupt in 1982

facts.statement: A specimen designated FSAC-OB 14 from the Maastrichtian-aged Ouled Abdoun Basin in Morocco was assigned to aff. Quetzalcoatlus in a 2018 study.
facts.quote: The Moroccan specimen, from the Ouled Abdoun Basin (Maastrichtian), is designated as FSAC-OB 14 and was assigned to aff. Quetzalcoatlus by a 2018 study.

facts.statement: In 2019, all azhdarchid remains from the Dinosaur Park Formation were revised as distinct from Quetzalcoatlus and named the new genus Cryodrakon.
facts.quote: In 2019, however, all azhdarchid remains from the formation were revised as distinct from Quetzalcoatlus and named as the new genus Cryodrakon.

facts.statement: A 2025 study found a Wyoming neck vertebra to be anatomically compatible with Q. lawsoni but forming a polytomy with Q. lawsoni, Q. northropi, and a Moroccan specimen in phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: The 2025 Infernodrakon study found it to be distinguishable from that taxon, but anatomically compatible with Q. lawsoni; when tested in a phylogenetic analysis, they found it to form a polytomy with Q. lawsoni, Q. northropi, and a Moroccan specimen.

facts.statement: A 2025 revision by Emily Thomas and Skye N. McDavid recovered Quetzalcoatlus as polyphyletic, finding Q. lawsoni does not clade with the type species Q. northropi.
facts.quote: Emily Thomas and Skye N. McDavid, in 2025, performed a revision of Azhdarchomorpha which recovered Quetzalcoatlus as polyphyletic, with Q. lawsoni not clading with the type species Q. northropi.

facts.statement: Specimens from across Late Cretaceous North America were historically assigned to Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: Several specimens from across Late Cretaceous North America were historically assigned to Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus northropi was among the largest azhdarchids, rivalled in size by Arambourgiania, Hatzegopteryx, and possibly Cryodrakon.
facts.quote: Quetzalcoatlus northropi was among the largest azhdarchids, though was rivalled in size by Arambourgiania and Hatzegopteryx (and possibly Cryodrakon).

facts.statement: Based on limb morphology and azhdarchid tracks from South Korea, Quetzalcoatlus was likely quadrupedal.
facts.quote: Based on the limb morphology of Q. lawsoni, related azhdarchids such as Zhejiangopterus, and pterosaurs at large, in addition to azhdarchid tracks from South Korea, Quetzalcoatlus was likely quadrupedal.

facts.statement: Azhdarchid wings had an aspect ratio of 8.1, similar to storks and birds of prey, indicating reliance on thermals and updrafts for soaring.
facts.quote: The aspect ratio of azhdarchid wings is 8.1, similar to that of storks and birds of prey that engage in static soaring, meaning they are reliant on thermals, updrafts, and other air currents to gain altitude through lift and remain aloft.

facts.statement: Recent estimates based on azhdarchid proportions place the wingspan of Quetzalcoatlus at 10 to 11 meters.
facts.quote: More recent estimates based on greater knowledge of azhdarchid proportions place its wingspan at 10 – 11 m.

facts.statement: Large azhdarchids like Q. northropi are estimated to have a shoulder height of 2 to 3 meters, with heads held at heights exceeding 4 meters.
facts.quote: Large azhdarchids such as Q. northropi have been estimated to have a shoulder height of about 2–3 m; the head may have been held at a height of more than 4 m, similar to that of an extant giraffe.

facts.statement: In 2021, Kevin Padian and colleagues estimated Q. northropi weighed around 150 kg and Q. lawsoni weighed 20 kg.
facts.quote: In 2021, Kevin Padian and colleagues estimated that Q. northropi would have weighed around 150 kg, and that Q. lawsoni would have weighed 20 kg

facts.statement: It cannot be determined whether indeterminate azhdarchid remains from Big Bend represent separate animals from Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: Whether any of these remains represented separate animals from Quetzalcoatlus cannot be determined.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Quetzalcoatlus were discovered in 1971 in Texas by Douglas A. Lawson.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles de Quetzalcoatlus fueron descubiertos en Texas, en la formación Javelina en el Parque nacional Big Bend (datado de hace cerca de 68 millones de años en el Maastrichtiense) en 1971 por un estudiante graduado de geología de la Escuela Jackson de Geociencias de la Universidad de Texas en Austin, Douglas A. Lawson.

facts.statement: Lawson announced the discovery in a 1975 article in the journal Science.
facts.quote: Lawson en 1975 anunció el hallazgo en un artículo en la revista Science.

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus was an extinct azdarchid pterosaur genus that lived between 68 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Quetzalcoatlus, llamado así por la deidad azteca Quetzalcóatl, la serpiente emplumada, es un género extinto de pterosaurio azdárquido del Cretácico superior, entre 68 a 66 en millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus was a member of the Azhdarchidae family, characterized by being toothless pterosaurs with rigid and unusually long necks.
facts.quote: Era un miembro de los azdárquidos, una familia de avanzados pterosaurios sin dientes con cuellos rígidos e inusualmente largos.

facts.statement: Analysis of cranial material shows Quetzalcoatlus had a very sharp and pointed beak, contrary to early reconstructions that depicted a blunt snout.
facts.quote: El análisis de la material craneal (de una especie menor aún innombrada) muestra que Quetzalcoatlus tenía un pico muy agudo y afilado, contrariamente a las primeras reconstrucciones que mostraban un hocico romo

facts.statement: A cranial crest was present, but its exact shape and size remain unknown.
facts.quote: Una cresta craneal estaba presente pero su forma y tamaño exactos son aún desconocidos.

facts.statement: A cervical vertebra of an azdarchid discovered in 2002 in the Hell Creek Formation of the Maastrichtian may also belong to Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: Una vértebra cervical de un azdárquido, descubierta en 2002 en la formación Hell Creek del Maastrichtiano, puede pertenecer también a Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: Quetzalcoatlus was abundant in Texas during the Lancian in a fauna dominated by Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: Quetzalcoatlus fue abundante en Texas durante el Lanciano en una fauna dominada por Alamosaurus.

facts.statement: The Alamosaurus-Quetzalcoatlus association likely represents interior semi-arid plains.
facts.quote: La asociación Alamosaurus-Quetzalcoatlus probablemente representa planicies semiáridas interiores.

facts.statement: Smaller specimens are more complete than the Q. northropi holotype, include four partial skulls, are much less massive, and have an estimated wingspan of 5.5 meters.
facts.quote: Los especímenes son más completos que los del holotipo de Q. northropi, e incluyen cuatro cráneos parciales, aunque son mucho menos masivos, con una envergadura estimada de 5.5 metros.

facts.statement: Specimen BMR P2002.2 was recovered accidentally when it was included in a plaster-covered block prepared to transport part of a tyrannosaurid specimen.
facts.quote: El espécimen (BMR P2002.2) fue recuperado accidentalmente cuando éste fue incluido en un bloque recubierto de yeso preparado para transportar parte de un ejemplar de un tiranosáurido.

facts.statement: The bone comes from an azdarchid pterosaur individual with an estimated wingspan between 5 and 5.5 meters.
facts.quote: El hueso viene de un individuo de pterosaurio azdárquido con una envergadura estimada entre 5 a 5.5 metros.

facts.statement: While some studies have yielded extremely low weight figures for Quetzalcoatlus, as low as 70 kilograms for a 10-meter individual, most estimates published in the 2000s have been higher, tending toward 200-250 kilograms.
facts.quote: Mientras que algunos estudios han arrojado cifras extremadamente bajas para el peso de Quetzalcoatlus, tanto como apenas 70 kilogramos para un individuo de 10 metros, la mayoría de estimaciones publicadas en la década de 2000 han sido mayores, y tienden hacia los 200 - 250 kilogramos.

facts.statement: In 2010, Mark Witton and colleagues considered the remains indistinguishable from the contemporary Romanian Hatzegopteryx.
facts.quote: Mark Witton y colegas en 2010 han considerado que los restos son indistinguibles de su contemporáneo rumano Hatzegopteryx.

facts.statement: If Q. northropi is sufficiently complete to be distinguished from other pterosaurs (or otherwise would be a nomen dubium), Hatzegopteryx may represent the same animal.
facts.quote: Si Q. northropi está lo suficientemente completo como para ser distinguido de otros pterosaurios (o de otra manera sería un nomen dubium), Hatzegopteryx puede representar el mismo animal.

facts.statement: Mark Witton et al. noted that the cranial material of Hatzegopteryx and Q. sp. differ too much to be considered the same animal, making it probable that if Q. sp. is not identical to Quetzalcoatlus northropi, it represents a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Mark Witton et al. señalaron que el material craneal de Hatzegopteryx y de Q. sp. difieren demasiado como para ser considerados del mismo animal, lo que haría probable que si Q. sp., no es idéntico a Quetzalcoatlus northropi, representa entonces un género distinto.

facts.statement: In 1975, Lawson rejected a piscivorous lifestyle, suggesting instead that Quetzalcoatlus was a scavenger like the modern vulture, feeding on the carcasses of titanosaurian sauropods like Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: Lawson en 1975 rechazó un estilo de vida piscívoro, sugiriendo en cambio que Quetzalcoatlus era un carroñero como el moderno marabú, alimentándose de los cadáveres de saurópodos titanosaurianos como Alamosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1996, Thomas Lehman and Langston rejected the scavenger hypothesis, noting that the lower jaw angled so strongly downward that even when fully closed there was a gap of more than five centimeters between it and the upper jaw, very different from the hooked beaks of specialized scavenger birds.
facts.quote: En 1996, Thomas Lehman y Langston descartaron la hipótesis del carroñero, señalando que la mandíbula inferior se inclinaba tan fuertemente hacia abajo que, aun cuando se cerrara completamente quedaba un espacio de más de cinco centímetros entre ésta y la mandíbula superior, muy distinto de los picos ganchudos de las aves carroñeras especializadas.

facts.statement: They suggested that with its long neck vertebrae and long toothless jaws, Quetzalcoatlus fed like modern skimmers, catching fish in flight while skimming the waves with its beak.
facts.quote: Ellos sugirieron que con sus largas vértebras del cuello y largas mandíbulas desdentadas Quetzalcoatlus se alimentaba como los actuales rayadores, atrapando peces en vuelo mientras surcaba las olas con su pico.

facts.statement: In 2008, pterosaur researchers Mark Paul Witton and Darren Naish published an examination of possible feeding habits and ecology of azdarchids.
facts.quote: En 2008 los investigadores de pterosaurios Mark Paul Witton y Darren Naish publicaron un examen de posibles hábitos de alimentación y ecología de los azdárquidos.

facts.statement: Witton and Naish noted that many azdarchid remains are found in continental deposits far from seas or other large bodies of water required for fishing.
facts.quote: Witton y Naish notaron que muchos restos de azdárquidos son hallados en depósitos continentales alejados de los mares u otros grandes cuerpos de agua requeridos para pescar.

facts.statement: Additionally, the beak, jaw, and neck anatomy are distinct from any animal that fishes in full flight.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, la anatomía del pico, mandíbula y cuello son distintos de cualquier animal que pesque en pleno vuelo.

facts.statement: Therefore, they concluded that azdarchids were probably terrestrial predators, similar to modern herons, and likely hunted small vertebrates on land or in small streams.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, ellos concluyeron que los azdárquidos eran probablemente depredadores terrestres, similares a las modernas cigüeñas, y probablemente cazaban pequeños vertebrados sobre tierra o en pequeños arroyos.

facts.statement: Although Quetzalcoatlus, like other pterosaurs, was quadrupedal when on the ground, Quetzalcoatlus and other azdarchids had limbs with proportions more similar to modern running ungulate mammals than their smaller relatives, implying they were uniquely adapted to a more terrestrial life.
facts.quote: Aunque Quetzalcoatlus, como otros pterosaurios, era un cuadrúpedo cuando estaba en tierra, Quetzalcoatlus y otros azdárquidos tenían extremidades con proporciones más similares a las de los modernos mamíferos ungulados corredores que sus parientes menores, implicando que estaban adaptados de manera única a una vida más terrestre.
